findings.body:
**Keep lint diagnostics on stderr.**

I1 applies to operation invocations, not this CI gate. However, this script documents human narration on stderr, while line 89 forwards lint output to stdout. Move that output to stderr. Do not add a JSON result.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-if (lint.stdout) process.stdout.write(lint.stdout);
+if (lint.stdout) process.stderr.write(lint.stdout);
```

</details>
findings.title: Keep lint diagnostics on stderr.

findings.body:
**Build `PATTERNS_REL` with POSIX separators so the allowlist and leak check work on Windows.**

`path.relative` returns `\`-separated paths on Windows. Two checks then fail:

- Line 117: `PATTERNS_ALLOW_RE` matches literal backslashes, for example `policy\\denylist\\patterns\.yml`. Gitleaks reports `/`-separated paths, so the allowlist entry does not match. The tree scan can then report the patterns file as a finding.
- Line 714: the leak filter converts `f.File` to `/` separators and then calls `.endsWith(PATTERNS_REL)` with the `\` form. On Windows that match cannot succeed, so the `leaked` check always passes. The self-test therefore cannot detect a finding inside the copied patterns file.

The script already treats Windows hosts as a supported case. The `probe_path` guards at lines 241-243 and 269-274 exist so that probe placement succeeds on Windows. The script also requires `/` separators for `probe_path` because gitleaks reports POSIX paths. `PATTERNS_REL` should follow the same rule. Line 693 can keep `path.join`, because `path.join` accepts `/` segments.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-const PATTERNS_REL = path.relative(REPO_ROOT, PATTERNS_PATH);
+// POSIX-separated: gitleaks reports '/'-separated paths, and the leak filter
+// normalizes findings to '/', so the allowlist regex and endsWith() must too.
+const PATTERNS_REL = path.relative(REPO_ROOT, PATTERNS_PATH).split(path.sep).join('/');
```

</details>
findings.title: Build `PATTERNSREL` with POSIX separators so the allowlist and leak check work on Windows.
